Hi Liam — thanks for the note and sorry for the confusion. This is a pretty common Google Calendar gotcha when invites are forwarded: the forwarded .ics sometimes loses the TZID anchor and appears to 'float' relative to the recipient's calendar settings.

To avoid that, I created a fresh invite anchored to UTC and attached a corrected-demo.ics file. Proposed slots (all shown in UTC):
- Tue 2027-06-01 14:00 UTC (10:00 ET / 00:00 AEST next day)
- Wed 2027-06-02 16:00 UTC (12:00 ET / 02:00 AEST next day)
- Thu 2027-06-03 08:00 UTC (04:00 ET / 18:00 AEST same day)

If any of those work, let me know which one you prefer and I'll update the Google Calendar event (and send the explicit .ics). I also included a small troubleshooting note below you can forward to your Sydney infra team to prevent floating times:

Troubleshooting checklist for forwarded invites:
- Prefer "Add to calendar" from the original invite instead of downloading & importing .ics.
- If forwarding, include the original event URL (calendar link) rather than forwarding the .ics file.
- Ask recipients to check their Google Calendar timezone (Settings > Time zone) and ensure DST is set to auto-update.

Attaching: corrected-demo.ics (explicit TZID), mutual_action_plan.pdf (short pre-demo checklist).

Thanks — I can host the demo and will invite Karthik to cover integration questions.

Best,
